# PLS-DA Evaluation
## Set up the data for analysis
```{r}
## Import all results
initial_data <- list(
    "all_binary_1000" = read.csv("results/triangle/mixed_all/plsda_1000_all.csv"),
    "all_binary_1250" = read.csv("results/triangle/mixed_all/plsda_1250_all.csv"),
    "all_weighted_1000" = read.csv("results/triangle/mixed_all/weighted_plsda_1000_all.csv"),
    "all_weighted_1250" = read.csv("results/triangle/mixed_all/weighted_plsda_1250_all.csv"),
    "austrian_binary_1000" = read.csv("results/triangle/austrian/plsda_1000_all.csv"),
    "austrian_binary_1250" = read.csv("results/triangle/austrian/plsda_1250_all.csv"),
    "austrian_weighted_1000" = read.csv("results/triangle/austrian/weighted_plsda_1000_all.csv"),
    "austrian_weighted_1250" = read.csv("results/triangle/austrian/weighted_plsda_1250_all.csv")
)

# remove all column except 1 - 5 and 15
data <- lapply(initial_data, function(df) df[, c(1:6, 10:13, 17,18)])

# add details about the sample_weight
data <- Map(function(df, nm) {
  df$Sample_weight <- if (grepl("weighted", nm, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    "TRUE"
  } else {
    "FALSE"
  }
  df
}, data, names(data))

## add details about the dataset
data <- Map(function(df, nm) {
  df$Dataset <- if (grepl("austrian", nm, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    "Austrian"
  } else {
    "All"
  }
  df
}, data, names(data))

# combine all dataframes into one
combined_data <- do.call(rbind, data)

# except F1_Score and MCC, transform all to factor
combined_data[c(1:6, 13,14)] <- lapply(combined_data[c(1:6, 13,14)], as.factor)
str(combined_data)

#Add TPR and TNR
combined_data$TPR <- combined_data$TP / (combined_data$TP + combined_data$FN)
combined_data$TNR <- combined_data$TN / (combined_data$TN + combined_data$FP)

#rename the columns
library(dplyr)
lme_data <- combined_data %>%
 rename(
   Grinding = Sample_source,
   Toxin = Target_toxin,
   Weighting = Sample_weight
 )
```

## Analysis using Linear mixed-effects on F1-Score
This experiment is performed using Full Factorial Design with 6 factors: Grinding, Toxin, Preprocessing, Variable_Selection, Downsampled, Dataset and Weighting. The model includes all main effects and interactions up to the three-way level. The random effect is Split, which accounts for the variability across different data splits.

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(glmmTMB)
library(car)

# The F1_Score is a proportion, so we can use a beta regression with logit link function. However, since we have random effects, we will use glmmTMB which can handle beta regression with random effects.
model_f1 <- glmmTMB(F1_score ~ Grinding + Toxin + Preprocessing + Variable_Selection + Downsampled + Dataset + Weighting + (1|Split), data = lme_data, family = ordbeta(link = "logit"),
control = glmmTMBControl(optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)))
Anova(model_f1, type = "II")
summary(model_f1)

# determine the ICC (intraclass correlation) of the model
library(performance)
icc(model_f1)
r2(model_f1)

# Get marginal means for all combinations
pipeline_means <- emmeans(model_f1, 
                          ~ Grinding * Toxin * Preprocessing * 
                            Variable_Selection * Downsampled * 
                            Dataset * Weighting)

# Convert to dataframe and back-transform to probability scale
pipeline_df <- as.data.frame(pipeline_means) |>
  mutate(
    pipeline = paste(Grinding, Toxin, Preprocessing,
                     Variable_Selection, Downsampled,
                     Dataset, Weighting, sep = " | "),
    F1_est   = plogis(emmean),
    F1_lcl   = plogis(asymp.LCL),
    F1_ucl   = plogis(asymp.UCL)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(F1_est))

# Get indices of top 10
top10_idx <- order(as.data.frame(pipeline_means)$emmean, 
                   decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
top10_means <- pipeline_means[top10_idx]

# Pairwise contrasts among top 10
library(multcomp)
cld_top10 <- cld(top10_means,
                            adjust  = "sidak",
                            Letters = letters,
                            sort    = TRUE) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    pipeline = paste(Grinding, Toxin, Preprocessing,
                     Variable_Selection, Downsampled,
                     Dataset, Weighting, sep = "\n"),  # newline for plot
    F1_est   = plogis(emmean),
    F1_lcl   = plogis(asymp.LCL),
    F1_ucl   = plogis(asymp.UCL),
    .group   = trimws(.group),
    # Flag pipelines in the top group
    is_best  = .group == .group[which.max(F1_est)]
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(F1_est))

# ============================================================
# STEP 4: VISUALIZATION 1 — TOP 10 WITH SIGNIFICANCE LETTERS
# ============================================================
library(forcats)
p1 <- cld_top10 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(pipeline, F1_est),
             y = F1_est,
             color = is_best)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = F1_lcl, ymax = F1_ucl),
                width = 0.25, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = .group, y = F1_ucl + 0.005),
            vjust = -0.3, size = 4, 
            color = "black", fontface = "bold") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = "#1a9850", "FALSE" = "steelblue"),
    labels = c("TRUE"  = "Best group",
               "FALSE" = "Other"),
    name   = ""
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      min(cld_top10$F1_lcl) - 0.01,
      max(cld_top10$F1_ucl) + 0.02
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Top 10 Pipelines by Estimated F1 Score",
    subtitle = "Shared letters = not significantly different (Sidak adjusted)\nGreen = statistically best group",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Estimated F1 Score",
    caption  = "Error bars = 95% CI | Results back-transformed from log-odds"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 9),
    axis.text.y   = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

print(p1)

```

### Plotting

```{r}
library(ggpubr)
library(viridis)
density_plot <- function(data, var, color, label, title){
  plot <- ggplot(data, aes(x = var, fill = color)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
    theme_classic() +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 5)) +
    labs(title = title, x = label, fill = color) +
    scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE) +
    theme(legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank())
  return(plot)
}

f1_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, color = "F1_Score", label = "F1 Score", title = "F1 Score of all pipelines") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("F1_Score" = "#DBA41A")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_weighting_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, lme_data$Weighting, label = "F1 Score", title = "Effect of Weighting") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_downsampled_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, lme_data$Downsampled, label = "F1 Score", title = "Effect of Downsampling") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_toxin_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, lme_data$Toxin, label = "F1 Score", title = "Effect of Toxin") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_dataset_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, lme_data$Dataset, label = "F1 Score", title = "Effect of Dataset") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_grinding_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, lme_data$Grinding, label = "F1 Score", title = "Effect of Grinding") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_preprocessing_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, lme_data$Preprocessing, label = "F1 Score", title = "Effect of Preprocessing") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_variable_selection_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, lme_data$Variable_Selection, label = "F1 Score", title = "Effect of Variable Selection") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_plots <- ggarrange(f1_plot, f1_weighting_plot, f1_downsampled_plot, f1_toxin_plot, f1_dataset_plot, f1_grinding_plot, f1_preprocessing_plot, f1_variable_selection_plot,
          ncol = 4, nrow = 2)
ggsave("./figures/PLS_DA/f1_density_plots.svg", f1_plots, width = 12, height = 6)
```

## Analysis using Linear mixed-effects on MCC

```{r}
# Transform MCC to be between 0 and 1 for beta regression
lme_data <- lme_data %>%
  mutate(MCC_scaled = (MCC + 1) / 2)
str(lme_data)

#Fit the linear mixed-effects model until three-way interaction
model_mcc <- glmmTMB(MCC_scaled ~ (Grinding + Toxin + Preprocessing + Variable_Selection + Downsampled + Dataset + Weighting)^3 + (1|Split), data = lme_data , family = ordbeta(link = "logit"), control = glmmTMBControl(optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)))
Anova(model_mcc, type = "II")
summary(model_mcc)

# determine the ICC (intraclass correlation) of the model
library(performance)
icc(model_mcc)
r2(model_mcc)

#select the best pipelines
pipeline_means_mcc <- emmeans(
  model_mcc,
  ~ Grinding * Toxin * Preprocessing *
    Variable_Selection * Downsampled *
    Dataset * Weighting
)

# Back-transform to response scale
# If MCC_scaled:  plogis() then rescale back: x * 2 - 1
pipeline_df_mcc <- as.data.frame(pipeline_means_mcc) |>
  mutate(
    pipeline = paste(Grinding, Toxin, Preprocessing,
                     Variable_Selection, Downsampled,
                     Dataset, Weighting, sep = " | "),

    # back-transform:
    MCC_est = plogis(emmean) * 2 - 1,
    MCC_lcl = plogis(asymp.LCL) * 2 - 1,
    MCC_ucl = plogis(asymp.UCL) * 2 - 1
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(MCC_est))

# Preview top 10
cat("\n=== TOP 10 PIPELINES (MCC) ===\n")
head(pipeline_df_mcc, 10)

# ============================================================
# STEP 6: PAIRWISE CONTRASTS AMONG TOP 10
# ============================================================

top10_idx_mcc <- order(
  as.data.frame(pipeline_means_mcc)$emmean,
  decreasing = TRUE
)[1:10]

top10_means_mcc <- pipeline_means_mcc[top10_idx_mcc]

top10_contrasts_mcc <- contrast(
  top10_means_mcc,
  method = "pairwise",
  adjust = "sidak"
)
summary(top10_contrasts_mcc)

# ============================================================
# STEP 7: COMPACT LETTER DISPLAY
# ============================================================

cld_top10_mcc <- multcomp::cld(
  top10_means_mcc,
  adjust  = "sidak",
  Letters = letters,
  sort    = TRUE
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    pipeline = paste(Grinding, Toxin, Preprocessing,
                     Variable_Selection, Downsampled,
                     Dataset, Weighting, sep = "\n"),
    MCC_est  = plogis(emmean),
    MCC_lcl  = plogis(asymp.LCL),
    MCC_ucl  = plogis(asymp.UCL),
    .group   = trimws(.group),
    is_best  = .group == .group[which.max(MCC_est)]
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(MCC_est))

# ============================================================
# STEP 8: VISUALIZATION 1 — TOP 10 WITH CLD LETTERS
# ============================================================

p1_mcc <- cld_top10_mcc |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(pipeline, MCC_est),
             y = MCC_est,
             color = is_best)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = MCC_lcl, ymax = MCC_ucl),
                width = 0.25, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = .group, y = MCC_ucl + 0.005),
            vjust = -0.3, size = 4,
            color = "black", fontface = "bold") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = "#1a9850", "FALSE" = "steelblue"),
    labels = c("TRUE" = "Best group", "FALSE" = "Other"),
    name   = ""
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      min(cld_top10_mcc$MCC_lcl) - 0.01,
      max(cld_top10_mcc$MCC_ucl) + 0.03
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Top 10 Pipelines by Estimated MCC",
    subtitle = "Shared letters = not significantly different (Sidak adjusted)\nGreen = statistically best group",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Estimated MCC",
    caption  = "Error bars = 95% CI | Results back-transformed from log-odds"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 9),
    axis.text.y     = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

print(p1_mcc)

# ============================================================
# STEP 9: VISUALIZATION 2 — CONTRAST HEATMAP
# ============================================================

contrast_df_mcc <- summary(top10_contrasts_mcc) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    significant = p.value < 0.05,
    sig_label   = case_when(
      p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE            ~ "ns"
    ),
    pipeline1 = sub(" - .*", "", contrast),
    pipeline2 = sub(".* - ", "", contrast)
  )

all_pipes_mcc <- unique(c(contrast_df_mcc$pipeline1,
                           contrast_df_mcc$pipeline2))

mat_df_mcc <- bind_rows(
  contrast_df_mcc |>
    select(pipeline1, pipeline2, p.value, sig_label),
  contrast_df_mcc |>
    rename(pipeline1 = pipeline2,
           pipeline2 = pipeline1) |>
    select(pipeline1, pipeline2, p.value, sig_label)
) |>
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(pipeline1 = all_pipes_mcc,
               pipeline2 = all_pipes_mcc,
               p.value   = 1,
               sig_label = "")
  )

p2_mcc <- mat_df_mcc |>
  ggplot(aes(x = pipeline1, y = pipeline2, fill = p.value)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sig_label),
            size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low      = "#d73027",
    mid      = "#ffffbf",
    high     = "#f7f7f7",
    midpoint = 0.05,
    limits   = c(0, 1),
    name     = "p-value"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Pairwise Comparison Heatmap — Top 10 Pipelines (MCC)",
    subtitle = "Red = significant difference | *** p<0.001 | ** p<0.01 | * p<0.05 | ns",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 7),
    axis.text.y     = element_text(size = 7),
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 8),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

print(p2_mcc)
```

```{r}
# Load your libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr) # For the comparison stars

# 1. Main Effect Plot
# Load your libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)

# Create the beautiful Violin + Boxplot combo
ggplot(lme_data, aes(x = Grinding, y = MCC, fill = Grinding)) +
  # The violin layer (trim = FALSE keeps the beautiful natural tails)
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.7, trim = FALSE, color = NA) +
  # The tiny inner boxplot (width = 0.1 keeps it slim)
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, fill = "white", color = "black", outlier.shape = NA) +
  # Your custom colors
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "#fca311", "TRUE" = "#14213d")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of MCC by Weighting",
    subtitle = "Violin shapes show the full density of your 12,800 data points",
    x = "Was Weighting Applied?",
    y = "MCC Score"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    legend.position = "none" # Hide the legend for a cleaner look
  ) +
  # Adding those helpful significance stars back in!
  stat_compare_means(
    comparisons = list(c("FALSE", "TRUE")), 
    label = "p.signif", 
    method = "t.test"
  )

# 2. Interaction Plot (Swapping X and Fill for cleaner brackets)
ggplot(lme_data, aes(x = Toxin, y = MCC, fill = Weighting)) +
  # Dodged violins to sit them next to each other
  geom_violin(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), alpha = 0.7, trim = FALSE, color = NA) +
  # Dodged inner boxplots
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.1, fill = "white", color = "black", outlier.shape = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "#fca311", "TRUE" = "#14213d")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Density of MCC Scores by Toxin and Weighting",
    x = "Toxin Type",
    y = "MCC Score",
    fill = "Weighting Applied?"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  # Adding the stars for the groups
  stat_compare_means(
    aes(group = Weighting), 
    label = "p.signif", 
    method = "t.test"
  )

str(mcc_pipelines_df)

library(ggplot2)

library(emmeans)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Calculate the marginal mean for JUST Weighting
emm_weighting <- emmeans(model_f1, ~ Toxin, pbkrtest.limit = 12800)
emm_weighting_df <- as.data.frame(emm_weighting)
str(emm_weighting_df)
# 2. Plot the isolated effect
ggplot(emm_weighting_df, aes(x = Toxin, y = emmean, color = Toxin)) +
  # Draw the error bar
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.1, size = 1) +
  # Draw the point estimate
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "#fca311", "TRUE" = "#14213d")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Main Effect of Weighting",
    subtitle = "Model-adjusted marginal means (with 95% CIs)",
    x = "Was Weighting Applied?",
    y = "Estimated MCC"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    legend.position = "none"
  )



library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Sort the dataframe from best to worst F1 Score
f1_ranked <- f1_pipelines_df %>%
  arrange(desc(emmean)) %>%
  mutate(Rank = row_number()) # Assign a rank from 1 to 128

# 2. Extract the lower confidence limit of the absolute BEST model (Rank 1)
threshold <- f1_ranked$lower.CL[1]

# 3. Categorize the models based on the Golden Rule
f1_ranked <- f1_ranked %>%
  mutate(
    Status = case_when(
      Rank == 1 ~ "The Best Model",
      upper.CL < threshold ~ "Significantly Worse than Best",
      TRUE ~ "Statistically Indistinguishable from Best"
    )
  )

# 4. Plot the ranked pipelines
ggplot(f1_ranked, aes(x = Rank, y = emmean, color = Status)) +
  # Add the error bars first so the points sit on top
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0, alpha = 0.5) +
  # Add the points
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  # Draw a horizontal dashed line at the threshold
  geom_hline(yintercept = threshold, linetype = "dashed", color = "darkred", size = 1) +
  # Custom colors for clarity
  scale_color_manual(values = c("The Best Model" = "#14213d", 
                                "Statistically Indistinguishable from Best" = "#fca311", 
                                "Significantly Worse than Best" = "gray70")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Ranking All 128 Pipelines by F1 Score",
    subtitle = "Models below the dashed red line are significantly worse than the top model",
    x = "Pipeline Rank (1 = Best, 128 = Worst)",
    y = "Estimated F1 Score",
    color = "Model Status"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

## Analysis using Linear mixed-effects on TPR and TNR
 
 ```{r}

model_tpr <- glmmTMB(TPR ~ (Grinding + Toxin + Preprocessing + Variable_Selection + Downsampled + Dataset + Weighting)^3 + (1|Split), data = lme_data, family = ordbeta(link = "logit"),
control = glmmTMBControl(optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)))
Anova(model_tpr, type = "II")

r2(model_tpr)

# Convert to dataframe and back-transform to probability scale

# Get indices of top 10

      min(cld_top10$tpr_lcl) - 0.01,
      max(cld_top10$tpr_ucl) + 0.02
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Top 10 Pipelines by Estimated TPR",
    subtitle = "Shared letters = not significantly different (Sidak adjusted)\nGreen = statistically best group",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Estimated TPR",
    caption  = "Error bars = 95% CI | Results back-transformed from log-odds"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 9),
    axis.text.y   = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

print(p1)


# Data analysis for TNR
model_tnr <- lmer(TNR ~ (Grinding + Toxin + Preprocessing + Variable_Selection + Downsampled + Dataset + Weighting)^3 + (1|Split), data = lme_data)
anova(model_tnr)
summary(model_tnr)

# select the best pipelines
best_pipelines_tnr <- emmeans(model_tnr, pairwise ~ Grinding * Toxin * Preprocessing * Variable_Selection * Downsampled * Dataset * Weighting, pbkrtest.limit = 12800)
tnr_pipelines_df <- as.data.frame(best_pipelines_tnr$emmeans)
tnr_pipelines_df <- tnr_pipelines_df[order(-tnr_pipelines_df$emmean), ]
```

tp_weighting_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$TPR, lme_data$Weighting, label = "True Positive Rate", title = "Effect of Weighting")
tp_toxin_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$TPR, lme_data$Toxin, label = "True Positive Rate", title = "Effect of Toxin")
